payload.previous_feedback: Previous vetter reason: The proof correctly establishes the floor decomposition x = floor(x) + frac(x) and the bounds 0 <= frac(x) < 1 for every real x. It matches the lemma exactly, with no missing steps or semantic drift.
payload.previous_proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer satisfying m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m throughout gives 0 <= x - m < 1. By the definition of the fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m. Hence 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Also, rearranging the identity frac(x) = x - floor(x) yields x = floor(x) + frac(x). Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
